$ stk connect github --device
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: github offers the device flow, but no client id is configured.

  the device grant identifies an OAuth app, and supertoolkit does not ship one —
  a shared client id would make every installation look like the same app.
  register your own, then add it to $ROOT/work/supertoolkit.yaml:

    services:
      github:
        device:
          client_id: <your app's client id>

  a client id is public by OAuth's design: it names an app and authorises
  nothing, so it is safe in a committed file. the stored token is what goes on the wire, so treat it as long-lived


$ stk connect nosuch --device
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: "nosuch" is not configured: run `stk add nosuch` first, which is also where the device client id goes


$ stk connect x --browser
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: x uses OAuth 2.0, but no client id is configured.

  supertoolkit ships no client id: a shared one would make every installation
  look like the same app. Register your own, add http://127.0.0.1:7837/callback as
  a redirect URI, then name the client id in $ROOT/work/supertoolkit.yaml:

    services:
      x:
        oauth2:
          client_id: <your app's client id>

  a client id is public by OAuth's design: it identifies an app and authorises
  nothing, so it is safe in a committed file. The client secret is not, so
  stk connect x --browser reads it from stdin.


$ stk connect github --browser
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: github does not use the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow.

  it uses substitute (token) — connect it with:
    stk connect github


$ stk connect github --device
exit 0
--- stdout

  connecting github without a browser on this machine
    1. $PROVIDER/device/code issues a short code
    2. you approve it in a browser, anywhere
    3. the token comes back here, to this broker only
    asking for: repo, read:org


  supertoolkit is connecting github
  code  WXYZ-1234
  open  https://example.invalid/device
  enter the code to approve it; it is useless to anyone who does not
  expires in $MINUTES

  waiting — checking every 1s, giving up at HH:MM UTC

  github connected · acquire (OAuth 2.0 refresh)
  sealed in $ROOT/state, never in $ROOT/work/supertoolkit.yaml
  granted: repo
  the access token expires YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
  a refresh token was issued and stored, so this renews itself without you
  the broker trades the stored refresh token for a short-lived access token; the refresh token only ever reaches the provider's token endpoint, never the API
--- stderr
